commentary: Market breadth sits at 50.0%, reflecting a split market where broad indices hold near record highs while rising interest rates apply downward pressure to fixed income duration. Bonds are currently failing to serve as an effective equity hedge as IEF, AGG, and TLT all trade below their 200-day moving averages amid 24-year high Treasury yields. The portfolio remains structured around high-momentum idiosyncratic risk winners in technology hardware and energy refining while anchoring the bond sleeve near its floor to limit duration drag. A drop in market breadth below 35% alongside bond funds recovering above their 200-day moving averages would prompt a shift toward defensively expanding the bond sleeve.
allocation_reason: The target bond weight of 0.28 sits 0.03 above the 0.25 sleeve minimum and 0.47 below the 0.75 maximum. With Treasury yields pressing higher and all three bond funds trading below their 200-day moving averages, fixed income is providing negative momentum rather than downside protection, justifying maintaining an allocation close to the lower limit.

decisions.thesis: QQQ demonstrates strong momentum with a 1m return of +6.1% and 12m return of +23.4%, sitting -1.1% off its high and above its 200d moving average with reasonable volatility of 18.2%. This performance indicates robust large-cap technology leadership in a split market, making it an ideal holding to bring total portfolio position count to the target of 15. Overlaps with existing broad market tech exposure in SPY, AAPL, AMZN, GOOGL, and NVDA.
decisions.risks: Tech sector valuation contraction or macroeconomic slowdown pushing price below 200d moving average.
decisions.reason_for_action: Completes portfolio count to target of 15 while capturing persistent growth momentum.
